text.p: A Texas man convicted of killing three teenagers in a botched 1982 murder-for-hire scheme was executed on Thursday in the second death sentence carried out here within 24 hours.

David Wayne Spence, 40, was sentenced to die after two Texas juries in separate trials found him guilty of stabbing the teens to death and dumping their bodies in a remote area of a lakeside park near Waco, Texas.

"My prayers go out to everybody. You all will have to understand that I do understand your pain. I didn't kill anybody. Maybe some way this will take the rage from you," Spence said before he was injected with a dose of lethal chemicals. He was pronounced dead at 7:32 p.m. EST.

Spence, along with two accomplices, was convicted of raping and killing Jill Montgomery, 17, after mistaking her for another woman they had been asked to kill in return for proceeds from a life insurance policy, prosecutors said.

Spence met Montgomery and her two friends, Raylene Rice, 17, and Kenneth Franks, 18, at a park on the banks of Lake Waco where they had gone to drink beer and smoke marijuana in July 1982, prosecutors said.

Thinking that Montgomery was the woman they had been hired to kill, Spence and his accomplices drove the three to a remote area of the park where they repeatedly raped the women and stabbed all three to death.
Spence's two accomplices, Gilbert and Tony Melendez, testified against him and were sentenced to consecutive life terms as part of a plea agreement with prosecutors.

Muneer Mohammad Deeb, 37, who prosecutors alleged had hired the men to kill a co-worker who spurned his advances, was initially sentenced to die for his role in the killings, but his case was retried and dismissed in January 1996.

Spence spent his final day on death row visiting with his brother, an ex-wife and some friends, and ate a last meal of fried chicken, french fries and chocolate ice cream. He was the fourth person executed in Texas this year and the 111th in the state since capital punishment resumed in 1982.
On Wednesday, Texas executed a former stockbroker who tried to commit suicide a day earlier by slashing his throat and wrist with the blade from a prison-issued disposable razor.
